items.claim: On counting-on, items written larger-first (big number stated first, 1-3 added) draw support more often than items written smaller-first, where the Learner must start from the larger addend given second.
The closing Problem of a Session is where performance drops. Still refuted: the final item, take-from-ten 10 - 2 at position 9, was first-try correct, and the last helped item fell at position 8.

Within make-a-ten, the items needing help have a larger addend of 7: this Session 5 + 7 ended in a Hint-assisted success (p67) and 4 + 7 in a Reveal (p68), and 7 + 6 ended in a Reveal in Session 7 (p57), while items with larger addend 8 or 9 were first-try correct (9 + 3 p64, 5 + 8 p65, 8 + 4 p66, 9 + 8 p55). Counter-cases exist: 7 + 6 was first-try correct in Session 6 (p50) and 4 + 7 in Session 7 (p54).

Teen-number decompose items (10 + ? = teen) are less secure than compose items. Still refuted: both decompose review items this Session, 10 + ? = 19 and 10 + ? = 14, were first-try correct with no help.
Teen decompose items with a larger ones part (e.g. 10 + ? = 15 or 16) draw support, while ones parts of 1-3 come on the first try.

The top of the unlocked ranges is now tested rather than assumed: wholes of 17-20 in Units 1-2, Unit 3 wholes of 15-20, counting-on with a teen larger addend in both orders, and teen compose and decompose at the top of 11-19.
Counting-on is reliable on the first attempt when the total stays at or below ten, and breaks down when the count runs past ten.
In unknown-addend subtraction with a teen whole, assistance appears when the answer requires going back across ten (the part taken is bigger than the ones digit), not when it stays above ten.
Partners to 10 are answered correctly on the first try in both missing-partner and take-from-ten form across the whole range of given partners, including the small-part take-from-ten direction.
Decomposing a teen number as ten plus some ones is secure: three of three first attempts correct, across 12, 14 and 19.

Teen-number decompose items (10 + ? = teen) are less secure than compose items. Refuted again: all three teen items this Session were first-try correct with no help, including two decompose items (10 + ? = 12 and 10 + ? = 16) spanning low and mid teens.
The Hints on counting-on are not tied to which addend is stated first; counting-on itself is the unfinished Skill, and success on it is currently about even regardless of the numbers.
On missed items the Learner goes to a Reveal rather than working through a Hint. Untested this Session: no item was missed on the first try, so neither Hints nor Reveals occurred.

Composing a ten and a small number (10 + n) is mostly secure; the one Reveal on 10 + 2 (p8) sits between two first-try correct compose Problems (p1, p9), so it looks isolated rather than a consistent gap.

Within make-a-ten, the largest sums draw help while smaller crossings stay clean. Refuted: 9 + 9 was first-try correct this Session after being revealed last Session, and 7 + 8 and 7 + 7 were also clean.
Because partners-to-10 and ten-plus-some-more are both first-try secure, the Learner will handle make-a-ten within 20 on first attempts without needing Hints.

Within teen numbers, composing (10 + n = ?) is less secure than decomposing (10 + ? = teen): decompose items have been first-try correct every time they have appeared, while compose items keep drawing an occasional hint before a correct answer (two more this Session, p21 and p25).
Help on make-a-ten appears only at the very top of the range, where both addends are 9 (sum 18), and not on other make-a-ten items.
Success on counting-on does not depend on the size of the total: past-ten items can be first-try correct while under-ten items need help.
Among middle-unknown items, the lapses fall on those where the first stated number is already ten or more, while middle-unknown items starting below ten are answered on the first try.

Counting-on is unreliable for this Learner except when the count is very short and the larger number comes first (like 9 + 1); it broke down when the larger addend came second and when the start number was already a teen.
Across all result-unknown structures, first tries land cleanly at wholes or totals up to about 15, and help comes at 19 and above.
Unknown-addend first attempts now hold up across the range of wholes sampled, from small wholes to high teens, in both the subtract and the missing-addend form.
Make-a-ten lapses are not tied to which addend is stated first or to the size of the larger addend; two near-identical smaller-first items with 9 split into a Reveal and a first-try correct.
Teen-number decompose items (10 + ? = teen) are less secure than compose items. Still refuted and untested this Session, since no teen-number items were given.
Subtraction from ten in the take-from-ten structure is mostly reliable but not perfect: eight of nine first attempts correct with no Hints, with one first-try miss (10 - 4) that ended in a Reveal.
Teen numbers in decompose form are answered correctly on the first try, including the top of the range (10 + ? = 19 first-try correct this Session, p70; 10 + ? = 17 last Session, p61).
Unknown-addend work is first-try correct on both the subtract structure and the missing-addend structure, across wholes all the way up to 20.
In partners-to-10, assistance appears when the partner the Learner must supply is small (1-3), while a missing partner of 4 or more is answered on the first try.

Unknown-addend items whose missing part is 1 or 2 are less secure than those whose missing part is 3 to 5: 13 + ? = 14 ended in a Reveal this Session (p109), while 15 - 12 (p103) and 10 + ? = 13 (p106), both missing 3, were first-try correct. The same item with a missing part of 1 was first-try correct in the previous Session (p100), so the pattern is not clean.
Unknown-addend first attempts mostly hold up across the range of wholes sampled, from small wholes to high teens, in both the subtract and the missing-addend form.

The closing Problem of a Session is where performance drops. Still refuted, but one data point returned: the final item this Session, take-from-ten 10 - 9 at position 9, was a first-try miss ending in a Reveal, while the previous Session's final item was clean.
Teen-numbers compose (10 + a small number) is reliable on first tries.
Teen-number decompose (10 + ? = teen) is handled as well as compose; the reverse direction is not a barrier.

Help this Session fell on items where the unknown or the amount joined was only 1 or 2 (10 + ? = 11, 9 + ? = 10, 15 + 2), while items with larger missing parts were clean; the subtract item 16 - 15, whose missing part is also 1, is a counter-example.

Unknown-addend items miss on the first try when the part given is below ten and the whole is above ten: 8 + ? = 12 was a first-try miss ending in a Reveal (p47) and 8 + ? = 11 was a first-try miss ending in a Hint-assisted success (p59), while 12 + ? = 13 (p60) and 11 - 10 = ? (p69), whose given parts are ten or more, were first-try correct.
The Unit 3 word-problem skills (result or total unknown, change unknown) will run about as cleanly as the Unit 2 skills, since no Unit 3 item had been attempted before this Session.
Within teen numbers, composing (10 + n = ?) is less secure than decomposing (10 + ? = teen).
Make-a-ten across ten is now mostly reliable on first attempts, at least in the larger-first structure.
Result-unknown has settled: after the first-exposure dip the items are first-try correct whatever the parts and whatever the form.

Within make-a-ten, the first-try misses have fallen on larger-first items while smaller-first items have been first-try correct: this Session 6 + 5 (Hint-assisted success after a first-try miss, p53) and 7 + 6 (Reveal, p57) were both larger-first, while smaller-first 4 + 7 (p54) and 6 + 6 (p58) were first-try correct, matching smaller-first 8 + 8 (p36) and 6 + 6 (p35) earlier. Larger-first 9 + 8 (p55) and 7 + 6 (p50) were also first-try correct, so the line is a tendency and not clean.

This Session's support appeared on items the Learner had answered cleanly in earlier Sessions (10 + 6, 7 + 1, 5 + 8), so the whole-Session dip may be day-to-day variation rather than a new gap in those Skills.
At the current mix of number sizes the Learner works without help across every unlocked Skill. Still refuted: three of nine items this Session needed a Hint before a correct answer.
Help on teen-number items is intermittent and not tied to any feature identified so far; which structure and which numbers it lands on changes from Session to Session.
Result-unknown transfers from the Unit 2 work: the Learner is first-try correct on add-to, take-from and put-together without Hints, including at wholes up to 20.
Partners to 10 and teen numbers being answered without help carried over to make-a-ten: first make-a-ten items were mostly first-try correct.
Help tends to land in the closing stretch of a Session, in the last third of the Problems.
The compose form of teen numbers (10 + 5 = ?) is the weakest spot in ten-anchored work.
Partners to 10 is secure across both structures: four more first-try correct items this Session (10 - 7, 10 - 2, 5 + ? = 10, 10 - 9) with no help needed.

Counting-on misses were tied to larger-first items whose sum crosses ten. Still refuted, and now contradicted from the other direction: this Session's only counting-on item was 8 + 1 (p121), a sum well below ten, and it ended in a Reveal.
Assistance now comes at one or two items per Session and lands on Unit 2 Skills (make-a-ten, counting-on) while Unit 3 items are first-try correct.

Counting-on help is not tied to the size of the larger addend or to the order of the addends; it appears across configurations. Weakened: the only counting-on item this Session, larger-first 15 + 3 with a teen larger addend, drew a Hint, which is also the pattern h7 now predicts.
Accuracy holds steady through the end of a Session rather than dropping at the late positions.
Subtraction written as a take-away (whole minus a part) is handled on the first try when the whole is under 10.

Misses are not tied to one Skill or one structure. Held again this Session: the three help events fell on three different Skills (Reveal on change-unknown 11 - ? = 7, p183; Hint on unknown-addend 13 + ? = 18, p184; Hint on make-a-ten 4 + 7, p186) while same-structure neighbours 9 - ? = 1 (p179) and 6 - ? = 5 (p181) were first-try correct. Confidence lowered because all three help items share the crossing-ten feature now under test as h27.
Counting-on addition is reliable on the first try whether or not the larger number comes first.
Review Problems draw help more often than planned Problems of the same Skills.
Unknown-addend items draw support even when the numbers match facts the Learner answers cleanly in other Skills, so the difficulty is with the unknown-addend format rather than the arithmetic.
Make-a-ten is now the skill carrying the residual difficulty: its first attempts draw misses and Reveals while the other skills come back first-try-correct.
All teen-number evidence so far is composing (10 + n = ?); decomposing a teen number into 10 and some ones has not been seen at all.
Partners to 10 is secure in both the missing-partner and take-from-ten structures: three first-try correct items with no assistance.

Within result-unknown, the items drawing help are the ones whose total crosses ten by combining two single-digit parts; totals at ten or below, and items that start from a ten, are answered on the first try.

On missed items the Learner goes to a Reveal rather than working through a Hint. Refuted: of four helped items this Session, three ended in Hint-assisted successes (10 + ? = 11, 9 + ? = 10, 15 + 2) and only one was a Reveal (3 + 4).

With partners to 10 and teen numbers both answered without help across a full Session, the Learner has the pieces the make-a-ten Skill is built on, so first make-a-ten items should mostly be first-try correct.
Inside make-a-ten, the items written with the smaller addend first draw help while larger-first crossing-ten items are answered on the first try.
Take-from-change runs about as cleanly as take-from in result-unknown.

On missed items the Learner goes to a Reveal rather than working through a Hint. Partly reopened: this Session two of three helped items ended in a Reveal (7 + 4 and 10 - 9) and one was a Hint-assisted success (8 + 7), reversing the previous Session's all-Hint pattern.

Within partners to 10, items with a large given number or a large amount taken away are less settled. Reopened as proposed: the one partners item this Session had a given number of 7 and went to a Reveal after a first-try miss.

The ten-based building blocks are largely in place and make-a-ten within 20 is still the growth edge, but this Session the help was spread wider: make-a-ten gave two first-try correct (p105, p110) and two Hint-assisted successes (p107, p108), while a teen decompose item needed a Hint (p102) and an unknown-addend item ended in a Reveal (p109); partners (p104) and counting-on (p101) stayed first-try correct.
Decomposing a teen number into 10 and some ones (10 + ? = teen) is as secure on first attempts as composing was.

Partners-to-10 is less stable than the Mastered estimate suggests: in Session 7 three of four partners-to-10 items needed help on the first attempt (Hint on p54, Reveals on p58 and p60) with only p57 first-try correct.
Make-a-ten and counting-on outcomes do not track how the addends are ordered on the page; the same structure comes out clean in one Session and non-clean in the next on both skills.
The items still not reached on the first try now fall mostly on the two Unit 3 Skills (result-unknown, change-unknown) rather than on the Mastered Unit 1 and Unit 2 Skills.
Within make-a-ten, items written smaller-first with 5 as the first addend draw assistance, while other make-a-ten framings are first-try correct.

Counting-on items where the amount counted on is 1 have drawn more help than items counting on 2 or 3. Still refuted and untested: the counting-on item this Session counted on 3 (5 + 3) and was first-try correct.

The top of the unlocked ranges is now tested rather than assumed: wholes of 17-20 in Units 1-2, Unit 3 wholes of 15-20, counting-on with a teen larger addend in both orders, teen compose and decompose at the top of 11-19, and change-unknown with a large change at a teen whole.

Teen-number decompose items (10 + ? = teen) are less secure than compose items. Still refuted: this Session both a decompose item (10 + ? = 17) and a compose item (10 + 7 = ?) were first-try correct, continuing a long clean run in both directions.

On missed items the Learner goes to a Reveal rather than working through a Hint. Strengthened slightly: of the three helped items this Session, two were Reveals (16 - 11, 7 + ? = 10) and one was resolved by Hint (15 + 3).
Compose form (10 + 5 = ?) is less secure than decompose form for teen numbers.

Counting-on misses were tied to larger-first items whose sum crosses ten. Still refuted, and the test still has not really run: this Session's only counting-on item was 9 + 1 (p101), first-try correct, with a sum of exactly ten.
Make-a-ten and subtraction-as-unknown-addend are available, since every item offered in each has been answered on the first try.
Make-a-ten items miss when the larger addend is 7 and hold when it is 8 or 9.
Make-a-ten is not yet settled: after a long run of first-try correct items, support reappears occasionally rather than the Skill being finished.
The top of the unlocked ranges is now tested rather than assumed: wholes of 17-20 in Units 1-2 and, as of this Session, Unit 3 wholes of 15, 18, and 20.
Unknown-addend problems are not yet available on a first attempt.

Within partners to 10, the take-from-ten form is currently less settled than the missing-partner form. Reopened as proposed: the take-from-ten item 10 - 9 was a first-try miss ending in a Reveal, and no missing-partner item appeared for comparison.
Unit 3 item types (result or total unknown) have not been attempted yet, so nothing is known about how the Learner handles them.
Unit 1 Skills lose their first-try reliability when they are absent from the planned diet for several Sessions; bringing them back will show first-attempt misses rather than clean work.
In unknown-addend, a missing part of 1 (the two given numbers sitting right next to each other) has drawn assistance every time it has appeared, in both the subtract and missing-addend forms.
Change-unknown needs assistance at a higher rate than any other Skill, even though other Skills also stumble.

Help falls on items written with the blank in the middle (a + ? = total, including teen decompose) more than on items with the blank at the end. Still refuted, now in the opposite direction: both middle-blank items were clean (10 + ? = 18, 9 + ? = 14) and all three helped items had the blank at the end (8 - 2, 2 + 14, 6 + 7).
Make-a-ten first attempts are now succeeding more often than not, with help down to about one item per Session.

Counting-on items where the amount counted on is 1 have drawn more help than items counting on 2 or 3. Reopened as proposed: this Session the plus-one item 8 + 1 was a first-try miss resolved by a Hint while the plus-two item 11 + 2 was first-try correct.

The Learner's fluency with partners to 10 and with 10 + n teen numbers carries over to new sums that cross ten (make-a-ten) and to subtraction framed as an unknown addend, without needing Hints on the first exposure.

Inside unknown-addend, the items that still draw help are the ones where the given part is below ten and the whole is above ten, so the count spans the ten; items whose numbers sit entirely on one side of ten are answered on the first try.

Work anchored on ten with the blank in the middle is reliable on first attempts: missing-partner to 10 (including partners 5, 6, 7), take-from-ten, and decompose of teens up to 19 have been first-try-correct every time.
Within the small wholes now being used, items written as subtraction (a - b = ?) draw support more often than items written as addition with a blank (a + ? = c).
Unknown-addend is the one Skill still producing assistance, and the assistance is scattered across both structures and all whole sizes rather than tracking any single surface feature.
Change-unknown draws Hints even at the smallest numbers, so the difficulty is not about the size of the whole: 5 + ? = 6 with a change of 1 was Hint-assisted.

The Learner can now run a whole Session clean: every item across ten-anchored, make-a-ten, unknown-addend and both Unit 3 word-problem skills was answered on the first attempt with no Hint or Reveal, including items that cross ten and wholes up to 20.
